## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded from the existing social support budget, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing and fewer appeals. A proposed first phase would cover three life events before expanding.

## What Makes It New

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, the time from life event to first payment, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the current application route would test whether uptake improves.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in and a clear record of which data was used. Wrong eligibility decisions would be reduced by keeping a human review step for edge cases.

## One-Sentence Summary

A single digital window where a new small business could get every license, permit, and registration it needs in one application instead of visiting several entities.

## Problem

Starting a small business often means repeating the same information to many different offices, waiting for approvals in sequence, and guessing which permits are needed. This delays openings and discourages people from starting businesses at all.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

First-time entrepreneurs opening small shops, cafes, home businesses, and service companies. A typical case is a person opening a small bakery who would need a trade license, a health permit, a signage permit, and civil defense approval.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes one online form that asks each question once and routes the answers to every relevant entity in parallel. A guided checklist would tell the applicant exactly which approvals their activity needs. A single case manager would be proposed for any application that gets stuck.

## Delivery Model

Delivered online with a helpdesk. Entities would connect through a shared data exchange.

## Funding & Sustainability

Fees would stay the same as today and be collected once and split between entities.

## What Makes It New

It brings many approvals together in one place.

## Measuring Impact

The plan is to track the number of days to open a business and the number of visits required.

## Risks & Mitigation

Entities may resist sharing data or changing processes; the initiative plans to start with a few willing entities.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed heat-safety program for outdoor workers that would combine hyper-local heat alerts, cooled rest shelters, and simple rules employers must follow on dangerous days.

## Problem

Outdoor workers in construction, delivery, and landscaping face serious health risks during extreme heat. General weather warnings are not specific enough to a worksite, and many workers feel unable to stop and rest without losing income.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Construction workers, delivery riders, cleaners, and gardeners who work outdoors, and the small employers who hire them. A delivery rider would receive an alert on a very hot afternoon showing the nearest cooled rest point.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes a heat-risk map combining temperature and humidity at neighborhood level, a network of cooled rest shelters at key locations such as fuel stations and parks, and a mobile alert for workers and employers. On high-risk days, employers would be asked to apply mandatory rest breaks, with guidance published in several languages.

## Delivery Model

Shelters would be proposed through partnerships with private sites, and alerts would go through a lightweight app and SMS. Inspectors would do spot checks on high-risk days.

## Funding & Sustainability

The plan is a shared model: the government would fund the alert system and a first set of shelters, and larger employers would be invited to sponsor additional shelters.

## What Makes It New

It moves from general weather warnings to worksite-level risk and pairs every alert with a practical place to rest.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include heat-related clinic visits among outdoor workers, shelter usage, and employer compliance on alert days.

## Risks & Mitigation

Workers may ignore alerts if they fear losing pay; the initiative plans to publish clear employer obligations. Shelter maintenance costs would be tested in a first phase.

## One-Sentence Summary

A program to reduce loneliness among seniors living alone by pairing them with trained volunteers and friendly daily check-in calls.

## Problem

Many elderly people living alone go days without speaking to anyone. Loneliness harms physical and mental health, and small problems such as a fall or missed medication can go unnoticed.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Seniors over 70 who live alone, and their families who live far away.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes daily automated check-in calls with a friendly voice, weekly visits from trained volunteers, and an alert to a family member or social worker if a senior does not answer or reports a problem.

## Delivery Model

Volunteers would be recruited from universities and community groups and trained by social services. The calls would be managed by a small central team.

## Funding & Sustainability

The plan is to fund the program from the social services budget, with volunteer time keeping costs low.

## What Makes It New

It combines technology with human contact.

## Measuring Impact

The initiative plans to measure loneliness scores and emergency response times.

## Risks & Mitigation

Volunteer drop-out is a risk; the plan is to offer recognition certificates.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed system where every rating a citizen gives after a government service would automatically create a follow-up task for the responsible team, with the result reported back to the citizen.

## Problem

Citizens are often asked to rate government services, but they rarely see anything change. Feedback is collected in dashboards that few people act on, so people stop giving honest feedback.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Every citizen and resident who uses government services, and the service managers who are responsible for improving them.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes that low ratings and written complaints would be grouped by topic using simple text analysis and sent to the named team responsible. Each team would be expected to respond within a set time. The citizen would receive a short message explaining what was changed because of their feedback, closing the loop.

## Delivery Model

Delivered through the existing rating screens in service centers and apps, with a shared task board for service managers.

## Funding & Sustainability

Funded from existing customer experience budgets; the main cost would be staff time to respond.

## What Makes It New

Most feedback systems stop at measuring. This one would make every complaint traceable to an action and tell citizens the result.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of complaints with a documented action, repeat complaints on the same topic, and whether citizens who get a response give feedback again.

## Risks & Mitigation

Teams may feel blamed; the initiative plans to present the system as a learning tool and to celebrate the teams that fix the most issues.

Short, paid, two-to-four-week project internships in government entities for university students, designed to give real work experience without a long commitment.

## Problem

University students in their second year or later, especially those without family networks to find internships.

The initiative proposes an online marketplace where government teams would post small, well-defined projects, and students would apply with a short task. Each completed project would give the student a digital certificate and a small stipend.

## Delivery Model

Run online, with a coordinator in each participating entity.

## Funding & Sustainability

Stipends would come from each entity's training budget.

## What Makes It New

The format is short and project-based rather than a long internship.

## Measuring Impact

The plan is to track the number of projects completed and student satisfaction.

## Risks & Mitigation

Teams may post low-value tasks; the initiative plans a simple review of each project before it is published.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed rewards program where households would earn points for correctly sorted recycling, redeemable for discounts on public transport and government service fees.

## Problem

Recycling rates remain low because sorting takes effort and people see no direct benefit. Contaminated recycling bins also increase processing costs.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Households in apartment buildings and villas, and building managers.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes smart recycling bins with a QR code scanner at collection points. Households would scan a personal code when depositing sorted recycling, and bins would estimate the weight and quality of the material. Points would be credited to a household account.

## Delivery Model

Delivered with waste collection companies that would install and operate the bins, and an app to show points.

## Funding & Sustainability

The plan is to fund rewards partly from the value of recovered materials and partly from savings in landfill costs.

## What Makes It New

It links recycling directly to benefits people already use, such as transport.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include recycling volume, contamination rate, and the number of active households.

## Risks & Mitigation

People may try to game the system with non-recyclable waste; the initiative plans random quality checks.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed home rehabilitation service where patients recovering from surgery or stroke would do guided physiotherapy at home through video sessions and simple motion-tracking on a phone.

## Problem

Many patients stop attending physiotherapy because travelling to a clinic several times a week is tiring, expensive, or impossible without help. Incomplete rehabilitation leads to slower recovery and more hospital readmissions.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or stroke, especially elderly patients and people living far from clinics, and the family members who support them.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes weekly live video sessions with a physiotherapist, plus daily exercises guided by a phone app that would use the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan.

## Delivery Model

Delivered by public hospital physiotherapy departments, with devices lent to patients who lack a smartphone.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded within existing hospital budgets, with the aim of lowering costs from readmissions and transport.

## What Makes It New

It brings rehabilitation into the home and uses the phone camera as a coach between sessions.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include completion rates of rehabilitation plans, mobility scores, and readmissions within 90 days, compared with clinic-based care in a planned trial.

## Risks & Mitigation

Some patients may struggle with technology; the plan is a first home visit to set up the device and train a family member.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed service that would detect water leaks inside homes from smart meter data and alert residents by SMS before they receive a high bill.

## Problem

Hidden leaks in homes waste large amounts of water and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing financial stress and disputes with the utility.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Households with smart water meters, especially elderly residents and families on low incomes for whom a surprise bill is a hardship.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes analysing hourly meter readings to spot continuous night-time water flow, which usually means a leak. Residents would receive an alert with simple steps to check for leaks and a link to book a subsidised plumber visit.

## Delivery Model

Delivered by the water utility through its existing meter data and customer channels.

## Funding & Sustainability

The plan is to fund the service from reduced water losses and fewer billing disputes.

## What Makes It New

It turns meter data that already exists into a protective service for residents.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include water saved, the number of leaks fixed after alerts, and the number of billing disputes.

## Risks & Mitigation

False alarms could annoy residents; the initiative plans to set a conservative detection threshold in a first phase.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed citizen co-design lab where small, randomly selected groups of residents would work with policy teams over several sessions to shape new policies before they are finalised.

## Problem

Policies are often designed without hearing from the people most affected, and public consultations tend to attract the same small group of highly engaged voices.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Residents from all backgrounds, selected randomly to reflect the population, and policy teams in government entities working on new regulations or services.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes that for selected policies, a group of about 25 residents would meet in four facilitated sessions, receive balanced information, hear from experts, and produce written recommendations. The policy team would be expected to publish a response explaining which recommendations were adopted and why.

## Delivery Model

Run by a small facilitation unit, with sessions held in community centers and online.

## Funding & Sustainability

Funded from a central innovation budget; participants would receive a small allowance for their time.

## What Makes It New

Random selection brings in voices that consultations usually miss.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of recommendations adopted, participant trust in government before and after, and diversity of participants.

## Risks & Mitigation

Recommendations may be ignored; the initiative plans to require a public written response for each one.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed service that detects life events such as the birth of a child, job loss, or retirement and would offer eligible families the relevant government support automatically, without an application.

## Problem

Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or the application requires documents from several entities. People in difficult moments, such as after losing a job, face the most paperwork at the time they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Families going through major life events: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. A typical use case is a mother who registers a birth and, within days, would receive a message listing the support she qualifies for, with one tap to accept.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that eligibility could be checked in the background when a life event is registered. The citizen would receive a clear message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the information already exists in government systems.

## Delivery Model

The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the eligibility rules, and each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability

The initiative plans to be funded from the existing social support budget, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing and fewer appeals. A proposed first phase would cover three life events before expanding.

## What Makes It New

Most government services wait for people to apply. This proposal reverses the direction: the government would come to the citizen at the moment of need, which is rare in social services.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible families receiving support, the time from life event to first payment, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the current application route would test whether uptake improves.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in and a clear record of which data was used. Wrong eligibility decisions would be reduced by keeping a human review step for edge cases.

A proposed heat-safety program for outdoor workers that would combine hyper-local heat alerts, cooled rest shelters, and simple rules employers must follow on dangerous days.

## Problem

Outdoor workers in construction, delivery, and landscaping face serious health risks during extreme heat. General weather warnings are not specific enough to a worksite, and many workers feel unable to stop and rest without losing income.

Construction workers, delivery riders, cleaners, and gardeners who work outdoors, and the small employers who hire them. A delivery rider would receive an alert on a very hot afternoon showing the nearest cooled rest point.

The initiative proposes a heat-risk map combining temperature and humidity at neighborhood level, a network of cooled rest shelters at key locations such as fuel stations and parks, and a mobile alert for workers and employers. ## Delivery Model

Shelters would be proposed through partnerships with private sites, and alerts would go through a lightweight app and SMS. Inspectors would do spot checks on high-risk days.

## Funding & Sustainability

The plan is a shared model: the government would fund the alert system and a first set of shelters, and larger employers would be invited to sponsor additional shelters.

## What Makes It New

It moves from general weather warnings to worksite-level risk and pairs every alert with a practical place to rest.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include heat-related clinic visits among outdoor workers, shelter usage, and employer compliance on alert days.

## Risks & Mitigation

Workers may ignore alerts if they fear losing pay; the initiative plans to publish clear employer obligations. Shelter maintenance costs would be tested in a first phase.

A proposed early wellbeing check for students that would use a short, private monthly questionnaire to help school counsellors spot students who may be struggling, before problems become serious.

Students aged 12 to 18 in public schools, their parents, and school counsellors.

Delivered through schools, with training for counsellors and a clear referral path to health services for serious cases.

The plan is to fund it from the education wellbeing budget.

## What Makes It New
It turns wellbeing support from reactive to early and gives counsellors a way to prioritise.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the number of students supported early, counsellor response times, and student-reported wellbeing over the school year.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy concerns from parents are a major risk; the initiative plans parental consent, strict data access rules, and no link to grades or discipline records.

Outdoor workers in construction, delivery, and landscaping face serious health risks during extreme heat. Construction workers, delivery riders, cleaners, and gardeners who work outdoors, and the small employers who hire them. Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. ## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that compound financial vulnerability, such as new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, and people with a newly registered disability. ## One-Sentence Summary
A proposed proactive service that identifies life changes in young adults and families through confidential self-reported check-ins, enabling schools and community hubs to automatically connect them with relevant government support and guidance without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Mental health and wellbeing difficulties among young people and families often go unnoticed until they affect daily life, work, or education. These challenges frequently coincide with, or are triggered by, major life events such as becoming a new parent, job loss, or financial strain. Many families who qualify for social support never receive it because they do not know it exists, the rules are hard to understand, or they face complex paperwork at the very moment they have the least energy for it.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
The service targets students in their final years of secondary education, recent graduates entering the workforce, and young families. It focuses on individuals experiencing major life transitions that impact wellbeing and stability, such as new graduates seeking employment, young parents, or individuals facing new financial pressures. A typical use case is a graduating student who reports feelings of anxiety about their future in a confidential check-in; the system would then connect them to career guidance, mental health resources, and potential income support, all presented as an offer they can accept with minimal steps.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a system where individuals, through regular, private check-ins conducted via trusted community channels like schools or community centers, can signal changes in their circumstances or wellbeing. When a potential need is identified, existing government records (with the person's explicit consent) would be linked in the background to check eligibility for relevant support. The individual would receive a clear, personalized message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or request to speak with a guidance counselor or case worker. No new documents would be requested when the necessary information already exists in government systems.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through established community institutions, primarily schools for students and recent graduates, and expanded to community hubs for young families. Staff such as school counsellors, career advisors, and community workers would be trained to introduce the check-in system and support individuals who opt in. Communication and service delivery would occur through a dedicated digital portal and SMS, with in-person support available for those who are not comfortable with digital tools.

The initiative is proposed to be funded from existing social support and youth wellbeing budgets, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced application processing, fewer appeals due to simplified access, and improved long-term outcomes that reduce demand on crisis services. This combination of early, preventative outreach and automated eligibility checking is rare in social and wellbeing services.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible young people and families receiving support, the time from a reported concern or life event to the connection with appropriate resources, user satisfaction with the process, and wellbeing outcomes over time. A planned comparison with the traditional application route would test whether uptake and timeliness of support improve.

A proposed service that proactively identifies outdoor workers facing imminent heat-risk events and automatically offers them access to mandated rest breaks, cooled shelters, and relevant support, without requiring a manual application.

## Problem
Outdoor workers in construction, delivery, and landscaping face serious health risks during extreme heat. General weather warnings are not specific enough to a worksite, and many workers feel unable to stop and rest without losing income. People in these dangerous moments face the greatest need for protection at the time they may have the least capacity or knowledge to navigate complex safety rules and support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Construction workers, delivery riders, cleaners, and gardeners who work outdoors, and the small employers who hire them. A typical use case is a delivery rider whose work route is forecast to enter a high-heat-risk zone, and who would then receive a clear alert and an automatic notification of their eligibility for a paid rest break and the location of the nearest cooled shelter.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes linking existing government and licensed weather data, with appropriate worker and employer consent, so that eligibility for heat-safety protections could be checked in the background when a high-risk forecast is confirmed for a specific worksite or zone. The worker and their employer would receive a clear message explaining the triggered protections (such as mandatory rest breaks), the location of the nearest cooled rest shelter, and any related income-support provisions they qualify for. They could accept, decline the specific shelter location, or ask a human advisor for help. No new documentation would be requested when work and location data already exist in permitted systems.

The service would be delivered through a lightweight government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for workers and employers who are not digital. Additionally, the service is proposed to be extended to include individuals experiencing significant housing insecurity or instability, a group often facing acute stress and complex support needs during life transitions.

The initiative proposes a system where individuals, through regular, private check-ins conducted via trusted community channels like schools or community centers, can signal changes in their circumstances or wellbeing. When a potential need is identified, existing government records (with the person's explicit consent) would be linked in the background to check eligibility for relevant support. The individual would receive a clear, personalized message explaining what they qualify for and why, and could accept, decline, or request to speak with a guidance counselor or case worker. No new documents would be requested when the necessary information already exists in government systems.

The service would be delivered through established community institutions, primarily schools for students and recent graduates, and expanded to community hubs for young families. Staff such as school counsellors, career advisors, and community workers would be trained to introduce the check-in system and support individuals who opt in. Communication and service delivery would occur through a dedicated digital portal and SMS, with in-person support available for those who are not comfortable with digital tools.

A planned comparison with the traditional application route would test whether uptake and timeliness of support improve.

## Problem
Mental health and wellbeing difficulties among young people and families often go unnoticed until they affect daily life, work, or education. It would then generate a personalized, plain-language summary of potential support pathways. The individual would receive a clear message explaining what they might qualify for and why, and could choose to initiate a formal eligibility check with their explicit consent, linking existing government records in the background. Staff such as school counsellors, career advisors, and community workers would be trained to introduce the check-in system and support individuals who opt in. # One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies, such as hidden water leaks, by analyzing smart meter data and, for eligible families experiencing major life events, automatically offers a bundled package of support including guided home-based therapies and financial relief, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A typical use case is a household on a low income where a hidden leak is detected; because the household is also identified as containing a patient recently discharged after a stroke, the residents would receive an alert and be automatically presented with a bundled package of support.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as options for subsidized repair, bill relief, or financial aid.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through the existing government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for people who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the rules linking utility data alerts and life-event data to support eligibility. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. ## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water). This proposal reverses the direction: by fusing operational data (like meter readings) with social support systems, the government would come to the citizen at the moment a hidden emergency is detected and proactively offer a pre-configured bundle of support. This combined approach of automatic, data-triggered outreach and bundled, home-based therapy is rare in public service delivery.

Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days, water saved, and the number of billing disputes avoided. # One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively identifies outdoor workers facing major life or health-related hardship events (such as the birth of a child, job loss, or hospital discharge requiring rehabilitation) and automatically offers them a bundled package of support, including mandated workplace protections, guided home-based therapies, and relevant social services, without requiring a manual application.

## Problem
Many families who qualify for social and health support services never receive them because they do not know the services exist, the rules are hard to understand, or the application process requires navigating paperwork from several different entities. People facing difficult moments, such as after a stroke or major surgery, often need rehabilitation most at the precise time they have the least energy for complex administrative tasks.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Construction workers, delivery riders, cleaners, and gardeners who work outdoors, and the small employers who hire them. A typical use case is a delivery rider whose work route is forecast to enter a high-heat-risk zone, and who would then receive a clear alert and an automatic notification of their eligibility for a paid rest break and the location of the nearest cooled shelter.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes linking existing government and licensed weather data, with appropriate worker and employer consent, so that eligibility for heat-safety protections could be checked in the background when a high-risk forecast is confirmed for a specific worksite or zone. The worker and their employer would receive a clear message explaining the triggered protections (such as mandatory rest breaks), the location of the nearest cooled rest shelter, and any related income-support or social service provisions they qualify for based on concurrent life events. They could accept, decline the specific shelter location, or ask a human advisor for help. No new documentation would be requested when work and location data already exist in permitted systems.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered by public hospital departments and relevant social agencies. For the rehabilitation or support component, devices would be lent to workers or their family members who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. The proactive offer and management of the bundled support package would be coordinated through a central digital channel, with SMS and a phone line maintained for those not comfortable with digital tools.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative plans to be funded from the existing workplace safety and social support budgets, with the aim of offsetting costs through reduced healthcare expenditures and fewer workplace injury claims. A proposed first phase would cover two high-risk heat scenarios before expanding to other weather-related hazards.

## What Makes It New
While most government services wait for people to find and apply for help, this proposal reverses the direction: by linking life-event data (with consent), the government would proactively come to the citizen at their moment of need with a pre-configured bundle of support, including health rehabilitation. This combined approach of automatic, event-triggered outreach and home-based, digitally guided therapy is rare in public service delivery.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of at-risk workers who receive and use triggered protections, the time from heat-risk alert to first rest-break compliance, and worker satisfaction. A planned comparison with areas using only general warnings would test whether health outcomes improve.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage and a clear record of which data was used for the alert. Wrong risk or eligibility decisions would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases and complex employment situations.

# One-Sentence Summary
A proposed service that proactively detects household utility emergencies, such as hidden water leaks, by analyzing smart meter data and automatically offers eligible outdoor workers streamlined access to subsidized support and financial relief.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems. Furthermore, the sudden financial shock of an unexpectedly high utility bill can destabilize household budgets, forcing difficult trade-offs between paying for essentials like food, medicine, or rent and addressing the urgent repair, thereby compounding the initial resource waste with broader social and economic vulnerability.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Construction workers, delivery riders, cleaners, and gardeners who work outdoors, and the small employers who hire them. A typical use case is a household of a delivery rider where a hidden leak is detected; the residents would receive an alert and, because their vulnerable status as outdoor workers is known to social services, be automatically presented with options for subsidized repair and bill relief.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes linking existing government records, with the person's consent, so that when a utility emergency like a continuous leak is detected via smart meter analysis, eligibility for support programs could be checked in the background. The citizen would receive a clear, unified message explaining the detected problem, the support they qualify for (such as a subsidized plumber visit or bill adjustment), and why, with a simple way to accept, decline, or ask a human case worker for help. No new documents would be requested when the relevant information already exists in government systems.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through a lightweight government app and SMS, with a phone line and service centers for workers and employers who are not digital. A small central team would maintain the rules linking utility data alerts to support eligibility, and each participating data entity (e.g., utilities, weather services, licensed employment platforms) would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability
The plan is to fund the service from reduced resource losses (like water) and fewer billing disputes, which offset the costs of the streamlined support and casework. A proposed first phase would cover a limited set of utility emergencies before expanding.

## What Makes It New
Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. This proposal reverses the direction: the system would proactively identify the at-risk worker and come to them at the moment of imminent danger with specific, actionable protections, which is rare in occupational health services.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, the time from leak detection to resolution, water saved, the number of billing disputes avoided, and citizen satisfaction. A planned comparison with the traditional route of residents discovering high bills and then seeking help would test whether financial stress is reduced and uptake of support improves.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage and a clear record of which data was used for the alert. Wrong eligibility decisions would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases and complex employment situations. To avoid annoyance, detection thresholds for alerts would be set conservatively in the first phase.
--- END PROJECT ---

A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies by analyzing smart meter data and, for eligible families experiencing major life events, automatically offers a bundled package of support including guided home-based therapies and financial relief, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A specific addition proposed is **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge, as these individuals often become the de facto patient support system while also facing new logistical and emotional burdens. A typical use case is a household where a hidden leak is detected; because the household is also identified as containing a patient recently discharged after a stroke, the residents would receive an alert and be automatically presented with a bundled package of support, which could also include resources for the informal caregiver.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered by public hospital departments and relevant social agencies. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. The proactive offer and management of the bundled support package, triggered by the fusion of utility data alerts and life-event data, would be coordinated through a central digital channel, with SMS and a phone line maintained for those not comfortable with digital tools. Each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and streamlined support.

## What Makes It New
Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. This proposal reverses the direction: by linking life-event and utility data (with consent), the system would proactively identify the at-risk household and come to them at the moment of imminent danger or acute need with a pre-configured bundle of specific, actionable protections and supports, which is rare in public service delivery.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days, water saved, and the number of billing disputes avoided. A planned comparison would test whether this proactive, bundled model improves uptake and outcomes and reduces financial stress compared to the current system where citizens must discover crises and seek out each service separately.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage and a clear record of which data was used for the alert. Wrong eligibility decisions would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases. To avoid annoyance, detection thresholds for utility alerts would be set conservatively in a proposed first phase.

# One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively identifies informal caregivers and individuals experiencing major life events, and automatically offers them a streamlined, single-application bundle of all relevant business licenses, permits, and financial support needed to start a home-based care or wellness business.

## Problem
Starting a small business, particularly in the care and wellness sector, often means repeating the same information to many different offices, waiting for approvals in sequence, and guessing which permits are needed. This delays openings and discourages people from starting businesses at all, creating a critical gap when individuals or families face new financial pressures due to a major life event.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs and a potential impetus for entrepreneurship: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after major medical events. A specific focus is proposed for **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge, who may seek to formalize their skills into a home-based care or wellness business. A typical use case is a person who, after becoming a primary caregiver, is automatically presented with a bundled package to start a small home business providing companion care or therapeutic services, because their new status is known to social services.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible individuals, the package would include a single application for every license, permit, and registration needed for their proposed home-based business, such as a trade license, health permit, and any required professional certifications. This business support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event, such as streamlined access to startup grants, financial aid, subsidized business coaching, and guided digital tools for managing client appointments and care plans.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through one online form that asks each question once and routes the answers to every relevant entity in parallel. A guided checklist would tell the applicant exactly which approvals their specific home-based business activity needs. A single case manager would be proposed for any application that gets stuck. Entities would connect through a shared data exchange. Support would also be available through a helpdesk and service centers for those not comfortable with digital tools.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing social support and economic development budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced demand on social assistance, more efficient application processing, and increased local economic activity and tax revenue. Savings from these avoided costs and new revenues are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and streamlined support.

## What Makes It New
Most government business services require entrepreneurs to navigate multiple siloed agencies to discover and claim their entitlements. This proposal reverses the direction: by linking life-event data (with consent), the system would proactively identify individuals at a life stage where starting a business could provide crucial stability and come to them with a pre-configured bundle of all specific, actionable licenses and financial supports in one application, which is rare in public service delivery.

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the reduction in the number of days and separate visits required to legally open a home-based care or wellness business, the share of eligible individuals who complete the bundled application after being proactively notified, the rate of business survival after one year, and improvements in household financial stability scores. A planned comparison would test whether this proactive, bundled model improves business launch rates and reduces administrative burden compared to the current system where citizens must discover each requirement and service separately.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage used to trigger the offer of support. Wrong eligibility decisions or business recommendations would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases. Resistance from entities to sharing data or changing processes would be mitigated by starting with a pilot involving a few willing entities and a limited set of business types.

Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. Mental health difficulties among young people often go unnoticed until they affect attendance, grades, or safety. School counsellors have many students and few ways to know who needs help first.

Students aged 12 to 18 in public schools, their parents, and school counsellors.

The initiative proposes a five-minute monthly questionnaire on a school device, based on validated wellbeing questions. Delivered through schools, with training for counsellors and a clear referral path to health services for serious cases.

The plan is to fund it from the education wellbeing budget. To enhance sustainability and manage scaling costs, the proposal includes a planned, tiered funding model. It turns wellbeing support from reactive to early and gives counsellors a way to prioritise.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the number of students supported early, counsellor response times, and student-reported wellbeing over the school year.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy concerns from parents are a major risk; the initiative plans parental consent, strict data access rules, and no link to grades or discipline records.

# One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively identifies individuals experiencing major life events and automatically offers them a streamlined, single-application bundle of all relevant licenses, permits, and financial support needed to start a home-based care or wellness business, while also detecting household utility emergencies to provide integrated financial relief.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs and a potential impetus for entrepreneurship: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after major medical events. A specific focus is proposed for **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge, who may seek to formalize their skills into a home-based care or wellness business. A typical use case is a person who, after becoming a primary caregiver, is automatically presented with a bundled package to start a small home business providing companion care or therapeutic services, because their new status is known to social services.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible individuals, the package would include a single application for every license, permit, and registration needed for their proposed home-based business, such as a trade license, health permit, and any required professional certifications. This business support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event, such as streamlined access to startup grants, financial aid, subsidized business coaching, and guided digital tools for managing client appointments and care plans. Additionally, by analyzing smart meter data with consent, the system would proactively detect household utility emergencies like hidden water leaks and automatically bundle financial relief for the unexpected bill and access to subsidized repair services into the same support package.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered through one online form that asks each question once and routes the answers to every relevant entity in parallel. A guided checklist would tell the applicant exactly which approvals their specific home-based business activity needs. A single case manager would be proposed for any application that gets stuck. Entities would connect through a shared data exchange. Support would also be available through a helpdesk and service centers for those not comfortable with digital tools. A small central team would maintain the rules linking utility data alerts and life-event registrations to support eligibility.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and streamlined support.

## What Makes It New
Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. This proposal reverses the direction: by linking life-event and utility data (with consent), the system would proactively identify the at-risk household and come to them at the moment of imminent danger or acute need with a pre-configured bundle of specific, actionable protections and supports, which is rare in public service delivery. **The novelty is further amplified by its cross-sectoral bundling logic. It proposes to move beyond single-issue, single-agency support by using a single life event as a unifying trigger to automatically assemble a multi-domain support package. This package would span health (rehabilitation), finance (aid for bills), infrastructure (repair services), and social care (caregiver respite), creating a unified, citizen-centric intervention from disparate departmental silos.**

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the reduction in the number of days and separate visits required to legally open a home-based care or wellness business, the share of eligible households receiving support after a utility alert, water saved, the number of billing disputes avoided, the share of eligible individuals who complete the bundled application after being proactively notified, and the rate of business survival after one year. A planned comparison would test whether this proactive, bundled model improves business launch rates, reduces administrative burden, and reduces financial stress compared to the current system where citizens must discover crises and seek out each service separately.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage and a clear record of which data was used for the alert or offer of support. Wrong eligibility decisions or business recommendations would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases. To avoid annoyance, detection thresholds for utility alerts would be set conservatively in a proposed first phase. Resistance from entities to sharing data or changing processes would be mitigated by starting with a pilot involving a few willing entities and a limited set of business types.

It turns wellbeing support from reactive to early and gives counsellors a way to prioritise.

Proposed indicators include the number of students supported early, counsellor response times, and student-reported wellbeing over the school year.

Privacy concerns from parents are a major risk; the initiative plans parental consent, strict data access rules, and no link to grades or discipline records.

In addition, a proposed expansion would target graduating students from public technical and care-focused training programs, as they transition into the workforce. A proposed early wellbeing check for students that would use a short, private monthly questionnaire to help school counsellors spot students who may be struggling, before problems become serious.

## Problem

Mental health difficulties among young people often go unnoticed until they affect attendance, grades, or safety. School counsellors have many students and few ways to know who needs help first.

Students aged 12 to 18 in public schools, their parents, and school counsellors.

The initiative proposes a five-minute monthly questionnaire on a school device, based on validated wellbeing questions. Delivered through schools, with training for counsellors and a clear referral path to health services for serious cases.

The plan is to fund it from the education wellbeing budget. To enhance sustainability and manage scaling costs, the proposal includes a planned, tiered funding model. It turns wellbeing support from reactive to early and gives counsellors a way to prioritise.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the number of students supported early, counsellor response times, and student-reported wellbeing over the school year.

Privacy concerns from parents are a major risk; the initiative plans parental consent, strict data access rules, and no link to grades or discipline records.

# One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies by analyzing smart meter data and, for eligible families experiencing major life events, automatically offers a bundled package of support including guided home-based therapies and financial relief, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A specific addition proposed is **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge, as these individuals often become the de facto patient support system while also facing new logistical and emotional burdens. The initiative also proposes to explicitly include **households in temporary or insecure housing**, such as those in social housing, emergency accommodation, or on short-term tenancies, as these residents are particularly vulnerable to the financial shock of a utility emergency and may lack the agency or resources to arrange repairs. A typical use case is a household where a hidden leak is detected; because the household is also identified as containing a patient recently discharged after a stroke and is in a temporary housing arrangement, the residents would receive an alert and be automatically presented with a bundled package of support, which could also include resources for the informal caregiver and specific protections against tenancy disruption due to the emergency.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered by public hospital departments and relevant social agencies. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. The proactive offer and management of the bundled support package, triggered by the fusion of utility data alerts and life-event data, would be coordinated through a central digital channel, with SMS and a phone line maintained for those not comfortable with digital tools. Each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and streamlined support.

## What Makes It New
Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days, water saved, and the number of billing disputes avoided. Wrong eligibility decisions would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases. # One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies by analyzing smart meter data and, for eligible families experiencing major life events, automatically offers a bundled package of support including guided home-based therapies and financial relief, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A specific addition proposed is **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge, as these individuals often become the de facto patient support system while also facing new logistical and emotional burdens. The initiative also proposes to explicitly include **households in temporary or insecure housing**, such as those in social housing, emergency accommodation, or on short-term tenancies, as these residents are particularly vulnerable to the financial shock of a utility emergency and may lack the agency or resources to arrange repairs. A typical use case is a household where a hidden leak is detected; because the household is also identified as containing a patient recently discharged after a stroke and is in a temporary housing arrangement, the residents would receive an alert and be automatically presented with a bundled package of support, which could also include resources for the informal caregiver and specific protections against tenancy disruption due to the emergency.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered by public hospital departments and relevant social agencies. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. The proactive offer and management of the bundled support package, triggered by the fusion of utility data alerts and life-event data, would be coordinated through a central digital channel, with SMS and a phone line maintained for those not comfortable with digital tools. Each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data.

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and streamlined support. **A proposed addition to the funding model is a targeted partnership with regulated utility companies, where a portion of the demonstrable savings from reduced water loss and avoided billing disputes is directly reinvested by the utilities into the program's operational costs. This would create a sustainable, performance-based funding stream tied directly to the value the initiative creates for the utility sector.**

## What Makes It New
Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. This proposal reverses the direction: by linking life-event and utility data (with consent), the system would proactively identify the at-risk household and come to them at the moment of imminent danger or acute need with a pre-configured bundle of specific, actionable protections and supports, which is rare in public service delivery. **The proposed initiative would differ meaningfully from existing services by moving beyond a single-agency, single-crisis response to a multi-agency, anticipatory bundling model. It would not just alert a household to a leak and offer a subsidy for repairs, but would, in the same proactive step, integrate support from health, social services, and housing agencies tailored to a detected major life event, creating a unified safety net triggered by a single data point.**

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days, water saved, and the number of billing disputes avoided. A planned comparison would test whether this proactive, bundled model improves uptake and outcomes and reduces financial stress compared to the current system where citizens must discover crises and seek out each service separately.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage and a clear record of which data was used for the alert. Wrong eligibility decisions would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases. To avoid annoyance, detection thresholds for utility alerts would be set conservatively in a proposed first phase.

## One-Sentence Summary

A proposed early wellbeing check for students that would use a short, private monthly questionnaire to help school counsellors spot students who may be struggling, before problems become serious.

## Problem

Mental health difficulties among young people often go unnoticed until they affect attendance, grades, or safety. School counsellors have many students and few ways to know who needs help first.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases

Students aged 12 to 18 in public schools, their parents, and school counsellors.

## Solution / Service Overview

The initiative proposes a five-minute monthly questionnaire on a school device, based on validated wellbeing questions. Answers would be seen only by the counsellor, who would receive a prioritised list of students to check in with. Students could also request a conversation directly through the tool.

## Delivery Model

Delivered through schools, with training for counsellors and a clear referral path to health services for serious cases.

## Funding & Sustainability

The plan is to fund it from the education wellbeing budget. To enhance sustainability and manage scaling costs, the proposal includes a planned, tiered funding model. Initial pilot implementation would be funded from the central education wellbeing budget. For subsequent wider rollout, a proposed co-funding model would be tested, where the central budget covers core platform licensing and training, while individual schools or their regional clusters would be responsible for funding the dedicated counsellor time required to administer the checks and conduct follow-up conversations. This approach is designed to ensure local ownership and long-term integration into school operations.

## What Makes It New

It turns wellbeing support from reactive to early and gives counsellors a way to prioritise.

## Measuring Impact

Proposed indicators include the number of students supported early, counsellor response times, and student-reported wellbeing over the school year.

## Risks & Mitigation

Privacy concerns from parents are a major risk; the initiative plans parental consent, strict data access rules, and no link to grades or discipline records.

# One-Sentence Summary
A proposed government service that proactively detects household utility emergencies by analyzing smart meter data and, for eligible families experiencing major life events, automatically offers a bundled package of support including guided home-based therapies and financial relief, without requiring a formal application.

## Problem
Hidden utility emergencies in homes, such as water leaks, waste large amounts of a critical resource and often go unnoticed until a very high bill arrives, causing severe financial stress and disputes with the utility. These crises create a moment of acute need where residents are least equipped to navigate complex support systems.

## Target Beneficiaries & Use Cases
Families going through major life events that create new support needs: new parents, people who recently lost their job, new retirees, people with a newly registered disability, and patients discharged after orthopedic surgery or a stroke. A specific addition proposed is **informal caregivers**, such as a family member assuming primary responsibility for an elderly relative after a hospital discharge, as these individuals often become the de facto patient support system while also facing new logistical and emotional burdens. The initiative also proposes to explicitly include **households in temporary or insecure housing**, such as those in social housing, emergency accommodation, or on short-term tenancies, as these residents are particularly vulnerable to the financial shock of a utility emergency and may lack the agency or resources to arrange repairs. A typical use case is a household where a hidden leak is detected; because the household is also identified as containing a patient recently discharged after a stroke and is in a temporary housing arrangement, the residents would receive an alert and be automatically presented with a bundled package of support, which could also include resources for the informal caregiver and specific protections against tenancy disruption due to the emergency.

## Solution / Service Overview
The initiative proposes a bundled support package delivered directly to the citizen. For eligible patients recovering from surgery or stroke, the package would include guided physiotherapy at home through scheduled live video sessions with a therapist and daily exercises guided by a simple phone app that uses the camera to count repetitions and flag incorrect movements. The therapist would review progress remotely and adjust the plan. This health support would be automatically bundled with other relevant supports triggered by the same life event and the detected utility emergency, such as financial aid for the unexpected bill, access to subsidized repair services, and caregiver-specific resources like respite care options.

## Delivery Model
The service would be delivered by public hospital departments and relevant social agencies. For the rehabilitation component, devices would be lent to patients who lack a smartphone, with a proposed initial home visit to set up the technology and train a family member if needed. The proactive offer and management of the bundled support package, triggered by the fusion of utility data alerts and life-event data, would be coordinated through a central digital channel, with SMS and a phone line maintained for those not comfortable with digital tools. Each participating entity would keep ownership of its own data. **The initiative proposes to pilot the delivery of the bundled support package through trusted, place-based intermediaries such as community health centers, public libraries, and social housing resident associations. These intermediaries would act as local hubs where citizens could receive in-person assistance to understand and activate their support package, access the loaned devices, and get help navigating the integrated services, thereby ensuring the digital-first coordination model does not exclude those with low digital literacy or trust.**

## Funding & Sustainability
The initiative proposes to be funded within existing hospital and social support budgets, with the aim of lowering long-term costs from reduced hospital readmissions, fewer missed therapies, more efficient application processing, and reduced resource losses (like water) and billing disputes. Savings from these avoided costs are proposed to offset the upfront costs of the technology, service integration, and streamlined support.

## What Makes It New
Most government safety programs issue general warnings and rely on workers or employers to know and claim their rights. This proposal reverses the direction: by linking life-event and utility data (with consent), the system would proactively identify the at-risk household and come to them at the moment of imminent danger or acute need with a pre-configured bundle of specific, actionable protections and supports, which is rare in public service delivery. **The proposed initiative would differ meaningfully from existing services by moving beyond a single-agency, single-crisis response to a multi-agency, anticipatory bundling model. It would not just alert a household to a leak and offer a subsidy for repairs, but would, in the same proactive step, integrate support from health, social services, and housing agencies tailored to a detected major life event, creating a unified safety net triggered by a single data point. A proposed key innovation is the use of the utility emergency as a 'tracer condition'—a non-medical, objectively measurable crisis that reliably signals a broader moment of vulnerability across multiple life domains, enabling the system to identify households in need of a multi-faceted intervention before they experience cascading failures.**

## Measuring Impact
Proposed indicators include the share of eligible households receiving support after an alert, completion rates of prescribed rehabilitation plans, improvements in patient mobility scores, the rate of hospital readmissions within 90 days, water saved, and the number of billing disputes avoided. A planned comparison would test whether this proactive, bundled model improves uptake and outcomes and reduces financial stress compared to the current system where citizens must discover crises and seek out each service separately.

## Risks & Mitigation
Privacy and consent are the main risks; the initiative proposes an explicit opt-in for data linkage and a clear record of which data was used for the alert. Wrong eligibility decisions would be mitigated by keeping a human review step for edge cases. To avoid annoyance, detection thresholds for utility alerts would be set conservatively in a proposed first phase.
--- END PROJECT ---
